text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Unofficial election results: Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) wins two thrids of the seats in the House of Counties.
- Is the government going to accept the car dealers' proposal to lower the car import tax to five from 15 percent?
- Young scientists to be awarded some 200 apartments by the city of Zagreb.
- Fred Hubbard, vice-president of the Bell-Tekstron Corp has confirmed the possibility of buying helicopter spare parts from the Karlovac gas turbine factory in the future.
- The government to vouch for entrepreneurial and artisans' loans of up to 1.4 million kuna under a new program of the state guarantee agency Razvitak.
- Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) to issue 100,000 German marks worth of bonds and offer them to foreign investors in May.
- Croatia among the six out 25 emerging countries that were awarded a good legal rating by the EBRD in a recently published study.
- We expected this victory, the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) vice-president Ivic Pasalic says in an interview.
- Local elections in Eastern Slavonia may be extended for yet another day, according UN Transitional Administration UNTAES.

- The times of the "wartime" newspapers such the weekly Globus are long gone by. We'll be following new European trends, Ninoslav Pavic, the owner of Europapress Holding tha published Globus, says in an interview. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
